stories.body: Iran’s leadership has vowed to push “enemy forces” from the Arabian Sea as tensions around the Strait of Hormuz continue. President Donald Trump said he expects talks with Tehran to resume next week, despite rejecting an Iranian proposal for a seven-day truce followed by the reopening of the strait. He also raised the possibility of further US air strikes, underscoring the uncertainty surrounding efforts to halt the conflict.
stories.headline: Iran tensions deepen as Trump rejects truce proposal but expects talks to resume

stories.body: Brent crude rose by more than 3% to near $108 a barrel after Trump rejected Tehran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the release of frozen Iranian funds, sanctions relief and renewed nuclear negotiations. Before the war, roughly a fifth of global oil supplies passed through the waterway, but commercial traffic has fallen sharply amid attacks on ships. Asian markets were mixed as traders weighed the risk of prolonged disruption.
stories.headline: Oil prices jump after Trump rejects Iran’s Hormuz reopening plan

stories.body: Ethiopia’s army chief has accused Eritrea and Sudan of supporting armed groups fighting federal forces as clashes with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front intensify. Sudan denied the allegation and accused Ethiopia of supporting Sudan’s rival Rapid Support Forces. Fighting resumed last week, reviving fears of a return to the 2020-22 civil war; drone strikes, communications disruptions and rebel advances into neighbouring regions have added to concern over civilian harm.
stories.headline: Ethiopia accuses Eritrea and Sudan of backing Tigray rebels

stories.body: Russian attacks killed eight people across Ukraine on Sunday and injured at least 22 people, including six children, in Kharkiv early Monday, according to Ukrainian authorities. Deaths were reported in Sumy, Odesa, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv, while residential buildings and civilian infrastructure were damaged. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia had launched more than 2,200 attack drones, 1,630 aerial bombs and 38 missiles over the previous week, while Moscow said it would continue its military campaign.
stories.headline: Russian strikes kill eight across Ukraine as Moscow vows to continue war

stories.body: Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally and its allies won 14 seats in France’s partial Senate elections, enough to form a Senate group for the first time. The result effectively quadruples the party’s representation in the 348-seat chamber and gives it greater funding and visibility before the 2027 presidential election. The Senate remains dominated by traditional right and centre-right forces, but the result signals the National Rally’s expanding support among local officials.
stories.headline: France’s National Rally wins record Senate representation

stories.body: Flooding has killed at least eight people in Thailand over the past 10 days and forced thousands into temporary shelters, even as rain eased in Bangkok. The capital was declared a disaster zone after a slow-moving low-pressure system brought sustained downpours and waist-high water to some streets. Authorities and forecasters warned that the heavy rainfall had caused widespread disruption in low-lying areas.
stories.headline: Thailand floods kill at least eight and displace thousands

stories.body: British counterterrorism police are questioning five men arrested near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire on suspicion of explosives offences and preparing a terrorist act. Police responded after reports of three suspicious vehicles travelling toward the base, which has recently been used by US aircraft involved in strikes on Iran. Bomb-disposal teams examined vehicles near the village of Whelford, a 400-metre cordon was imposed and nearby residents were evacuated; authorities said they believed the incident was contained.
stories.headline: Five men questioned after terrorism arrests near RAF Fairford

stories.body: Republicans in competitive races are increasingly criticising the disruption caused by Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations as the midterm elections approach. Recent enforcement actions have unsettled communities and businesses in Kansas, Texas, Florida, Michigan and Maine, prompting some GOP officials to call for closer coordination with local authorities and a focus on serious offenders. A Politico poll found 49% of US adults consider the administration’s mass-deportation campaign too aggressive, compared with 26% who say it is about right.
stories.headline: ICE operations become a political risk for vulnerable Republicans

stories.body: White House efforts to lower prices for US consumers have so far struggled to deliver results, according to reporting on the administration’s response to voters’ top economic concern ahead of the midterms. Proposed measures affecting goods ranging from beef to diesel have encountered resistance, illustrating the political and practical constraints on efforts to quickly reduce household costs.
stories.headline: White House consumer-price plans face resistance from beef to diesel

stories.body: Spain’s government is negotiating urgently to secure parliamentary support for a housing decree it hopes to approve on Tuesday, while housing activists stage an encampment in Madrid and mobilisations elsewhere. The proposed package includes stronger eviction protections, restrictions on speculative purchases by large investment funds, regulation of seasonal rentals, higher tax on tourist flats and incentives for tenants and landlords. Coalition partner Sumar says an agreement remains distant, and the decree would lapse unless Congress validates it within a month.
stories.headline: Spain races to secure backing for housing decree amid protests

stories.body: The Spanish government will replace its delegate in Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano, after he said he could no longer continue following what he described as sustained harassment, threats and a disinformation campaign after a major migrant influx in July. Pérez Triano said he had warned Madrid that migration pressure was worsening and requested reinforcements before the mass arrivals, while government sources said security officials had remained in contact and sent support before 30 July.
stories.headline: Government replaces Ceuta delegate after resignation over harassment

stories.body: Israel has summoned Spain’s chargé d’affaires to issue a reprimand over comments by Youth Minister Sira Rego, who said last week that Spaniards supported “a free Palestine from the river to the sea.” Israel’s foreign ministry said the remarks showed that Spain’s government had lost its moral compass. Diplomatic representation between the two countries has already been reduced.
stories.headline: Israel summons Spain’s top diplomat over minister’s Palestine remarks

stories.body: A prosecutor has criticised the speed with which Judge Juan Carlos Peinado moved to complete the investigation involving Begoña Gómez, the prime minister’s wife, before his retirement. In a filing concerning a challenge to a preliminary hearing called with roughly 24 hours’ notice, the prosecutor said the procedure was legally valid but that such haste was unusual and showed insufficient consideration for lawyers and other participants. The case will now be handled by the judge’s successor.
stories.headline: Spanish prosecutor criticises judge’s rushed handling of Begoña Gómez case

stories.body: Vicente Mompó, president of Valencia’s provincial council, told a congressional inquiry that the handling of the deadly 29 October 2024 floods was “a disaster.” The Popular Party official said he did not praise the actions of any public official that day, while repeating the regional government’s argument that authorities lacked sufficient information during the emergency.
stories.headline: Valencia provincial president calls 2024 flood response a disaster

stories.body: Housing groups blocked several Barcelona roads, including sections of Avinguda Meridiana and Creu Coberta, to press Pedro Sánchez’s government to approve a stronger national housing decree. Activists are demanding automatic lease renewals, rent freezes, action against allegedly fraudulent seasonal rentals and a lasting suspension of evictions for vulnerable people. The demonstrations coincided with Sánchez’s visit to the city and followed calls to intensify pressure before the cabinet considers the proposed decree.
stories.headline: Housing protests disrupt Barcelona during Sánchez visit

stories.body: Catalonia’s weather service has issued warnings for heavy rain from early Tuesday across coastal and pre-coastal counties, with a danger level of four out of six. Storms could bring more than 40 litres of rain per square metre in 30 minutes, more than 90 litres in three hours and locally as much as 150 litres. Authorities warned of possible local flooding and urged people to avoid streams and ravines and follow official guidance.
stories.headline: Catalonia warns of torrential rain along coast and pre-coastal areas

stories.body: Barcelona’s public transport operator TMB says replacing its 772 remaining fuel-powered buses with electric vehicles could save €66.5 million over their operating life, according to a study by the UPC’s transport innovation centre. Electrification would require substantially higher upfront spending on vehicles and charging infrastructure, but lower energy and maintenance costs would reduce the total long-term cost below that of conventional replacement. TMB ultimately aims for 90% of its fleet to run on electricity and the remainder on hydrogen.
stories.headline: TMB says full electrification of Barcelona bus fleet could save €66.5m

stories.body: National Police have dismantled a criminal network accused of producing and distributing cocaine in Catalonia and Aragon, with links to Italy. Five people were arrested, three of whom were remanded in custody, and officers shut down a clandestine cocaine laboratory in a Barcelona home. Searches recovered nine kilograms of cocaine, 11 kilograms of cannabis, chemical precursors, cash and a vehicle; investigators said the lab posed a particular risk because it operated inside a residential building.
stories.headline: Police dismantle cocaine network operating between Catalonia and Aragon
